headline.quick: Trace a parser: what does parse() return for 4 model replies?
headline.dungeon: Tutorials Dojo 20-question diagnostic, then a hanging agent loop and a container that cannot write

intel.title: Model output is untrusted input: fail loudly at the parse boundary
bullets: json.loads raises json.JSONDecodeError on anything that is not valid JSON. Single-quoted keys are not valid JSON.
JSONDecodeError is a subclass of ValueError. Catch that, not a bare Exception.
On a parse failure, do not return an empty dict. Send the error text back to the model as the tool result so it can correct itself.
Count every loop iteration, successful or not, so one bad reply cannot spin forever.
intel.why: Handling malformed tool arguments is the error path your Tree 1 boss fight requires, and it is the first thing to check when an agent hangs in production.

question.q: json.loads("{'a': 1}") - what happens, and which exception class should you catch?
question.a: It raises json.JSONDecodeError (a subclass of ValueError) because JSON requires double quotes. Catch json.JSONDecodeError, not bare Exception.

quests.title: Micro-drill: trace parse() by hand
quests.brief: No running code, no AI. Read lines 1 to 25 and predict what happens. Paper or the reMarkable is fine.
tasks: For each of the 4 strings in SCRIPTED, write down exactly what parse() returns.
For the one that differs, write one sentence saying why.
Write what call_model() returns when history contains zero assistant messages, and when it contains ten.
quests.done_condition: You have 4 written return values plus 2 call_model answers, and they match the answer key.
answer_key: Reply 3: {} - single quotes are not valid JSON, json.loads raises JSONDecodeError, and the bare except hides it.
call_model with zero assistant messages returns SCRIPTED[0]; with ten it returns SCRIPTED[3], because min() clamps the index to the last item.

quests.title: Diagnostic: 20 Tutorials Dojo questions, untimed
quests.brief: This sets your starting line for Tree 2. A low score is the useful result here: it tells tonight's build which domains to drill.
tasks: Open your Tutorials Dojo SAA-C03 practice exams and start the first set in Review Mode.
Answer the first 20 questions untimed, then stop. Do not look anything up.
For each miss, write one line: why the wrong option looked right to you.
Tally misses under the four exam domains: Secure, Resilient, High-Performing, Cost-Optimized architectures.
Type your score and your two weakest domains into the check-in fields below.
quests.done_condition: The check-in has a score out of 20 and at least one weak domain or topic typed in.

quests.title: Trace the full loop: find 3 planted bugs
quests.brief: This 44-line agent loop has three bugs. Find them by reading. Predict what the program prints before you run anything. AI autocomplete off.
tasks: Trace run() turn by turn. Keep a table: turn, reply, action, what happens to history and to turns.
Write your prediction: what does the program print, and when does it stop?
Write the line numbers of the three bugs and one sentence on each.
Now save it as trace01.py and run: timeout 3 python3 trace01.py; echo $?
Compare the exit code with your prediction, then open the answer key.
quests.done_condition: You have three line numbers written down before running it, and the exit code is 124.
answer_key: Lines 24-25: parse() swallows every exception and returns {}. A malformed reply is indistinguishable from an empty one.
Lines 37-38: the tool call's errors are swallowed and 'continue' skips the history append, so the model never learns that the call failed.
Lines 38 and 41: turns only increments on success, so max_turns does not bound a failing loop.

What actually happens: turn 1 succeeds (T-101). Reply 2 asks for T-999, get_status raises KeyError, 'continue' runs, history is unchanged, so call_model returns reply 2 again, forever. Nothing is printed. timeout kills it: exit code 124.
The single-quoted reply 3 is never reached, but it would hang the same way: parse() returns {}, then action['tool'] raises KeyError.

quests.title: War-Game 1: the container that cannot write
quests.brief: A customer runs your agent in rootless Podman on RHEL 9. After they moved the data directory it crashes at startup. They say: 'It worked yesterday. We already ran chmod 777. Can you just run it as root?' Set a 15-minute timer. Evidence is in the code block.
quests.code:
# old runbook (worked yesterday)
podman run --rm -v /home/svc-agent/data:/data:Z registry.example/agent:1.4

# new runbook (fails today)
$ podman run --rm -v /srv/agent-data:/data:rw registry.example/agent:1.4
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/state.db'

$ ls -ld /srv/agent-data
drwxrwxrwx. 2 svc-agent svc-agent 4096 Nov 26 09:14 /srv/agent-data

$ getenforce
Enforcing

$ sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent | tail -1
type=AVC msg=audit(1795914872.114:912): avc:  denied  { write } for pid=4121
  comm="python3" name="agent-data"
  scontext=system_u:system_r:container_t:s0:c123,c456
  tcontext=unconfined_u:object_r:var_t:s0 tclass=dir permissive=0
tasks: Write the 4-bullet RCA brief, one line each:
[C] Confirmed signal from the logs or symptoms. Facts only.
[?] The single highest-value command or check to verify it.
[Fix] The minimal reversible remediation. Also say in one line why you will not run it as root.
quests.done_condition: Four bullets are written, [C] contains no guesses, and your [?] is one command.
answer_key: [C] Write to /data fails with EACCES while the directory is mode 777, so Unix permissions are not the cause. SELinux is Enforcing and logged an AVC denial: container_t writing to a var_t directory.
[I] The new mount flag dropped ':Z', so /srv/agent-data kept its default var_t label and SELinux blocks the container.
[?] ls -Zd /srv/agent-data - expect var_t where container_file_t is needed.
[Fix] Put ':Z' back on the volume flag so Podman relabels the directory. Reversible with restorecon -R /srv/agent-data.
Not root, not setenforce 0, not more chmod: none of them address the label, and the first two remove a security control from the customer's host.
